# `btcaddr` — specification

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E2 A2 H3 P3 · limited by scope (core), hardening (fuzz/ct not all recorded), performance (not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

Bitcoin address layer: scriptPubKey <-> address, network detection, WIF, P2SH/P2WSH helpers,
over the `bech32` codec. Usage: see ./README.md. Attribution: `NOTICE` (Core test data only).

**Where we are ahead:** allocation-free with fixed buffers; honest network sets instead of
a silent testnet/signet/regtest guess; one typed error per rejection reason; WIF key range
check and secret scratch wiped; checked against Core's own 140-row corpus in both directions.
**Where we are behind:** no output descriptors, no P2TR key-path construction from an internal
key (needs the tweak — `bip340`/`taproot` layer), no address-type *policy* checks (dust,
standardness), no bech32 error location, no `Address` generic over "unchecked" phantom
state (→ Backlog).

## What this module is, and what it is not

Glue between three things that already exist: the `bech32` codec (segwit rules, base58check),
`ripemd160`'s `hash160`, and std SHA-256. It knows seven byte templates and four networks.
It does **not** interpret Script, derive keys, tweak taproot keys, test that a public key is
a curve point, or judge standardness. A script outside the templates is
`error.UnsupportedScript`, never a guessed address.

## Design & invariants

- **Networks are a set on decode, a value on encode.** testnet (3 and 4), signet and regtest share
  the base58 versions `0x6f` (P2PKH) / `0xc4` (P2SH) / `0xef` (WIF); testnet and signet share the
  `tb` HRP. Decoding returns `Chains` (a `packed struct(u4)`): `bc`/`0x00`/`0x05`/`0x80` ->
  `{mainnet}`, `tb` -> `{testnet, signet}`, `bcrt` -> `{regtest}`, other base58 ->
  `{testnet, signet, regtest}`. Bitcoin Core's `testnet4` chain is `Network.testnet` here (same
  bytes as testnet3). `toScriptPubKeyFor(addr, net)` is the "I know the network" form and returns
  `error.WrongNetwork`. Rejected alternative: a `Network` result with an arbitrary pick for
  the ambiguous cases — it makes callers believe a `tb1` string was a testnet address when it may
  be a signet one.
- **Templates (`classify`)**, exact match only: P2PKH `76 a9 14 <20> 88 ac`; P2SH `a9 14 <20> 87`;
  witness program = `OP_0` or `OP_1..OP_16`, then one direct push (`len == remaining`) of 2..40
  bytes. Version 0 must be 20 (P2WPKH) or 32 (P2WSH) bytes; version 1 with 32 bytes is P2TR;
  any other version/length in range is `witness_unknown` (BIP350 wants those addresses to
  round-trip). `OP_PUSHDATA*`, trailing bytes and P2PK / multisig / `OP_RETURN` are
  `UnsupportedScript`.
- **Address decoding order:** a `bc1`/`tb1`/`bcrt1` prefix (any case) goes to the segwit path, which
  reuses `bech32.decode` + `bech32.decodeSegwit` (variant rule, lengths, padding, mixed case,
  upper-case accepted per BIP173). Otherwise a string that is valid bech32 under a foreign HRP is
  `UnknownHrp`; anything else is tried as Base58Check (payload exactly 1 + 20 bytes, version one of
  `00 05 6f c4`, else `UnknownVersionByte` — a WIF key handed in as an address lands there).
- **WIF:** `version(0x80|0xef) ++ key32 [++ 0x01]`; the scalar must be in `[1, n-1]`
  (`InvalidKey`); a 34-byte payload whose last byte is not `0x01` is `InvalidCompressionFlag`.
  Base58 alphabet, checksum and the 128-byte bounds are `bech32.base58`'s.
- **Helpers** follow BIP16/141/143: P2SH redeem script <= 520 bytes; P2WSH witness script <= 10000
  bytes (consensus); P2WPKH and P2SH-P2WPKH require a compressed key (33 bytes, `02`/`03`);
  P2PKH also takes 65-byte `04` keys. Hybrid `06`/`07` keys are refused. Curve membership is not
  checked (that is `k256`'s question).
- Reentrant, no heap, no shared state. `deps`: `bech32`, `ripemd160`, std SHA-256.

## Limits and refusals

Script <= 42 bytes; address <= 90 characters (`bech32.max_len`); WIF <= 52 characters
(`max_wif_len`); redeem script 520, witness script 10000. Untrusted address lengths are bounded
before any O(n²) work by `bech32.base58` (`InputTooLong` / `BufferTooSmall`, mapped to
`InvalidPayloadLength` here).

## Threat model / out of scope

Address strings are attacker-controlled (QR scans, RPC parameters, paste): decoding never
allocates, panics or writes out of bounds and returns a typed error on every rejection path.
Base58Check's 32-bit checksum detects typos only; nothing here authenticates an address.
**WIF is secret material.** Inside this module the base58 digit buffer, the base58check staging
buffers (`bech32.base58` wipes them), the WIF payload scratch in `wifEncode` and the decode
scratch in `wifDecode` are wiped with `std.crypto.secureZero` on every exit (CONVENTIONS §2.1;
the compiler may still keep copies in registers or spill slots — the caveat of §2.1 applies).
What is left to the caller: `Wif.key` (`Wif.wipe()`) and the `out` buffer given to `wifEncode`.
`base58` is **not constant-time** in the secret (it inherits `bech32.base58`'s documented limit,
`alphabet[d]` indexed by payload digits); this module makes no constant-time claim. The address
side has no secrets.

## Verification

`scripts/modtest btcaddr`. `src/core_test.zig` runs every row of Bitcoin Core's
`key_io_valid.json` (70) and `key_io_invalid.json` (70) via the generated `src/core_vectors.zig`:
address rows both ways on the row's chain (script equality, the chain in the result set, mainnet
vs non-mainnet, re-encode equals the string, wrong-network rejection, upper-case bech32 for
`tryCaseFlip`, and the WIF decoder rejecting the address), WIF rows both ways with the
compressed flag, every invalid row rejected as address (`toScriptPubKey` and, for each of the four
networks, `toScriptPubKeyFor`) and as WIF. `src/unit_test.zig`: each typed reason, the network
sets, BIP173/BIP350 examples (P2WPKH, P2WSH, P2TR, v16), BIP143's P2SH-P2WPKH scriptPubKey, key
`1` WIF strings (mainnet/compressed/uncompressed/signet), helper limits, and the P2SH / P2WSH
helper results, whose expected values were derived independently with Python `hashlib`.

### Audit 2026-10-03

Review of `src/root.zig` (templates, both decode paths, WIF, helpers) against Bitcoin Core's
`key_io.cpp` behaviour and BIP16/141/143/173/350, plus the `bech32.base58` bounds it relies on. No
HIGH/MED/LOW defect found: every rejection path returns a typed error, scratch is wiped on every
exit, no input-controlled index or allocation exists. INFO only: (1) `keyInRange` (`root.zig`,
`std.mem.eql`/`order`) is not constant-time in the key; the module makes no such claim and the
check compares against a public constant, but a caller who needs it must not rely on this function.
(2) `wifEncode` needs only the encoded length in `out`, not `max_wif_len` as its doc says (a
10-byte buffer gives `BufferTooSmall`, a 51-byte one suffices for an uncompressed key).
(3) `Decoded.script_buf` / `Address.buf` bytes past `len` are undefined; use `script()` / `slice()`.

Mutation run (schemata, ReleaseSafe, one binary, 53 mutants on the template bytes, version-opcode
range, network versions / HRP / sets, decode path selection, WIF length / flag / key range, helper
bounds): 53 killed, 0 equivalent. The first pass left 11 alive: each fixed byte of the P2PKH and
P2SH templates (8 mutants: no test altered a single template byte), the witness-version range
edges `0x50` / `0x61` (OP_RESERVED / OP_NOP would have been read as v0 / v17), "any version with a
32-byte program is P2TR", and the `0x04` prefix check of 65-byte keys (hybrid `06`/`07`). Three
tests added in `src/unit_test.zig` (`classify: every byte ...`, `classify: the witness version
opcode ...`, `helpers: a 65-byte key must start with 0x04`); the 11 mutants were rerun and die.

## Backlog / deferred

- **Output descriptors** (`addr()`, `pkh()`, `wpkh()`, `tr()` …) — not now; needs a Script/miniscript layer above.
- **P2TR from an internal key** (BIP341 tweak) — belongs with `bip340`/`bitcointx`; this module takes the tweaked key.
- **"Unchecked" address type** (rust-bitcoin's `Address<NetworkUnchecked>`): a value type carrying the `Chains` set that must be `assume/require`d — the current `Decoded.chains` covers the information but not the type-level enforcement. Not now.
- **Non-standard-script hints** (P2PK, bare multisig, `OP_RETURN` data) as a typed `ScriptKind` instead of `UnsupportedScript` — never for addresses (they have none); maybe as `classify` extension if a consumer asks.
- **Public-key validation** via `k256` (point on curve) in the key helpers — not now: would add a dependency for a check most callers already made.
- **`witness_unknown` constructor** (`scriptWitness(version, program)`) — not now; `fromScriptPubKey` on hand-built bytes covers it.

## Status

`extract · any · codec · reentrant` + deps: `bech32`, `ripemd160` — canonical source is `pub const meta` in
src/root.zig.

## Anchoring

Facing a wire format other implementations must agree with, and tested against a foreign implementation's own corpus.

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

**What the tests actually contain.** Bitcoin Core's `key_io_valid.json` / `key_io_invalid.json`
(MIT), fetched from `bitcoin/bitcoin` `master` at `e7aef7e86da79000aa42f5ba6d13b0d123d9da7c`;
plus BIP143 / BIP173 / BIP350 published examples. The Core rows are converted by
`tools/gen_core_vectors.py` (kept: it is the recipe that produced the committed file, CONVENTIONS §9),
which records source commit and SHA-256 of both inputs in the generated header. Helper vectors
(P2SH of a 1-of-1 multisig, key `1` WIF) were derived with Python `hashlib`, a separate implementation.

**Not covered by an external oracle:** the `Chains` set semantics (Core has no such notion; the
test checks `contains(row chain)` and mainnet exclusivity, the set contents are asserted by hand in
`unit_test.zig`), and the range check of WIF scalars (Core's corpus holds no out-of-range key).
